texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provis ions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 2-5-2001 at about 6.30 PM Food Inspector B.P.Saroha purchased a sample of 'Guava Juice Drink' a food article for analysis from the accused No. 1 Sh.Vishwa Nath Da vs Vishwa Nath Batra Etc. on 8 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27942862/ 1 Batra at M/s Chefair The Pastry Shop, 13, Bengalow Road, Kamala Nagar, Delhi where the said food article was found stored for sale and the accused No.1 Sh.Vishwa Nath Batra was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling. The sample consisted of 6x250 ml sealed tin cane of Guava Juice Drink taken as such in originally sealed condition bearing identical label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh.Arun Mishra, SDM/LHA. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice was given to accused No. 1 Sh.Vishwa Nath Batra and the price of the sample was also given to him. Panchnama was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by FI B.P. Singh were signed by accused No. 1 Vishwa Nath Batra and the other witness Sh.S.P. Singh, Fl. Before starting sample proceedings efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward. 3. It is further stated that one counter-part of the sample was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc. the sample and found the sample to be misbranded. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows : "The sample is misbranded because the nature declared as Guava Juice Drink is misleading (fruit juice and fruit drink have different standards) further there is violation of rule 32 e, f and i." 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Vishwa Nath Batra was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Chefair The Pastry Shop, 13, Bengalow Road, Kamala Nagar, Delhi at the time of sampling and the vendor disclosed that he had purchased the sampled commodity from M/s Gee Ess Overseas, D-S, Malka Ganj, Delhi. It is further stated that M/s Gee Ess Overseas is a proprietorship firm and accused No. 2 Sh. Rajeev Kumar Sahni is the proprietor of the said firm and found to be incharge of and responsible for the day to day conduct of business of the said firm. 5. It is further stated that after conclusion of the investigation the entire case file including the statutory documents and PA's report and the FI's report were sent to the Director, PFA, Govt. of Delhi who had accorded Consent under section 20 of the PFA Act for instituting the case. After obtaining the Consent of Director PFA, the present case was filed before the Court on 29.08.2001 alleging violation of section 2(ia) (ix)(g)(k) of PFA Act read with rule 32 (e)(f)(i) pf PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16 of PFA Act. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc. persons were summoned vide order dated 29.08.2001. Accused no. 1 Vishwa Nath Batra expired during pendency of the proceedings and the proceedings against him stood abated. Based on the PA report, notice of accusation under Section 251 CrPC was framed against accused persons for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16 PFA Act, being violation of Rule 32 (e)(f)(i) and section 2 Da vs Vishwa Nath Batra Etc. on 8 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27942862/ 2 (ix)(g)&(k) of PFA Rules, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. During the trial accused no. 1 has passed away. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case. PW-1 SDM/LHA Arun Mishra, PW-2 FI B.P. Saroha and PW-3 FI S.P. Singh deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 02.05.2001 and narrated the steps undertaken by him during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 6x250 ml can of Guava Juice Drink in original sealed condition, dividing it in three parts by considering two packets as one counterpart, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witness. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, notice in Form VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, notice u/s 14 A Ex.PW1/D, counter parts of sample deposited vide receipt Ex.PW1/E & PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/F, PA report Ex. PW-1/G. After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-1/H was taken from the Director PFA and on the complaint Ex. PW-1/I was filed in the Court by PW-1. A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex.PW1/J was sent to the accused persons vide registration receipt Ex.PW1/K. DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc. 8. Statements of the accused no. 1 & 2 under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 09.06.2010 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. They chose to lead evidence in their defence. 9. In their defence, the accused No. 1 Vishwa Nath Batra examined himself as DW-1. Thereafter, vide order dated 30.05.2016 the defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: Section 19 of PFA Act categorically provides that it shall be no defence in a prosecution for an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food to allege merely that the vendor was ignorant of the nature, substance or quality of food sold by him. The vendor, however, can escape his liability under the provision of Section 19(2) of PFA Act which provides as under : "19.(2)) A vendor shall not be deemed to have committed an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food if he proves- (a) that he purchased the article of food - (i) in a case where a licence is prescribed for the sale thereof, from a duly licensed manufacturer distributor or dealer; (ii) in any other case from any manufacturer, distributor or dealer, with a written warrantee in the prescribed form; and (b) That the article of food while in his possession was properly stored and that he sold it in the same state as he purchased it. Rule 12-A of the Rules reads thus: "12-A. Warranty. - Every manufacturer distributor or dealer selling an article of food to a vendor shall give either separately or in the bill, cash memo or label, a warranty in Form VI-A," Da vs Vishwa Nath Batra Etc. on 8 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27942862/ 4 17.
